sentences.text: Learned members at the Bar have volunteered to assist the Court pro bono in the highest tradition of the profession.
The Court has appointed Shri Ajay Singh Yadav, learned counsel as amicus curiae.

By means of the the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 304 of 2018 at Police Station- Kydganj, District- Allahabad under Sections 342, 376, 354Kha,
354Gha IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 27.08.2018.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 26.09.2018.

The following arguments made by learned counsel as amicus curiae for the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The delay of two days in lodgment of the FIR in the facts and circumstances of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
2. Material contradictions in the FIR, statements under Section 161 CrPC, Section 164 CrPC discredit the prosecution case.
3. The eye witness who was 12 years old child has also been tutored by his parents and he is not reliable witness.
His version contradicts the prosecution case.
4. The father of the victim as well as the victim have refused to undergo internal medical examination as it would falsify the prosecution case.
5. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who always cooperated in the investigation and joined the trial proceedings.
He did not tamper with the evidence nor influenced the witnesses.
6. The clothes being worn by the victim were not produced before the Investigating Officer by the family members of the victim.
The mother of the victim had disposed of the clothes.
7. All the prosecution witnesses have been examined.
The applicant is disabled to tender effective defence of his case to refute the prosecution evidences due to his continued incarceration.
8. The applicant is not a flight risk.
There is no possibility of the applicant reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Sonu Nishad @ Shyamu Nishad be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.
The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
